text:
ashley: Quick sync — I'm about to apply a TF change that consolidates egress subnets across prod and staging for cost reasons. main changes: shrink public NAT subnets, move some nodegroups to a new egress-only subnet, and update route tables. Posting plan snippet, want quick eyes before I run apply.

ashley: plan shows replacement for aws_route_table_association.egress-rt-assoc (forces new association) and modify on aws_nat_gateway.* (no replacement). Concern: cross-account routes for analytics VPC peering.

mike: please paste the tf snippet for the route assoc and the module call. quick review. :eyes:

ashley: here —
```hcl
module "egress_subnet" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra-modules.git//network/egress-subnet"
  cidr = var.egress_cidr
  azs  = local.azs
}
resource "aws_route_table_association" "egress-rt-assoc" {
  subnet_id      = module.egress_subnet.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.egress.id
}
```

sanjay: two quick checks: 1) Are there any Immutable tags on the existing route table associations? We had a bug where an external process recreates associations if tags differ. 2) For peering -> analytics, did you set "propagate" or explicit routes?

ashley: 1) No immutable tags as far as I can see. 2) I'm adding explicit routes in the analytics account via remote-state var. plan shows adding `aws_route.analytics-to-egress` with destination = analytics CIDR via peering-id.

mike: re: NAT — ensure you keep one NAT GW per AZ for our HA requirement. If TF suggests deleting a NAT and recreating in a different subnet, that's a short outage window for new ephemeral EIPs. We should coordinate deploy window.

ashley: good point. I added lifecycle prevent_destroy on the NAT module in the branch; but TF still plans to replace assoc because old assoc referenced old subnet id. That will be a <5s bounce for nodegroup egress, but we should node-drain to be safe?

teresa: If node egress changes, pods with hostNetwork or fixed IPs might misbehave. Which nodegroups are moving?

ashley: only batch-worker-1 and batch-worker-2 (spot). Non-critical but they handle data exports. I'll schedule maintenance.

sanjay: also double-check Security Group rules for the new subnet: analytics IP ranges were only allowed from old egress CIDR. Update SGs or we'll break exports.

ashley: already updated the sg rule in the branch: `aws_security_group_rule.analytics-allow-egress` new cidr = var.egress_cidr. Plan shows it as an update.

infra-bot: TF plan summary — 4 to add, 2 to change, 3 to destroy. Proposed apply will touch: aws_route_table_association (replace), aws_security_group_rule (update), aws_route (add), aws_subnet (add), aws_subnet (destroy).

mike: ok — action items before apply:
- ashley: open PR and tag network-owners (done?)
- ashley: confirm peering route propagation policy with analytics (sanjay)
- ashley: schedule nodegroup drain for batch workers during apply window
- teresa: confirm SG change won't impact any internal tooling

ashley: PR opened: https://git.company/infra/compare/egress-reconcile. Tagged @network-team and @analytics. I'll wait for one more lgtm from infra before applying. Targeting tomorrow 03:00 UTC maintenance window.

sanjay: lgtm from analytics side assuming SG update lands in same apply. I'll watch peering route entries after apply and can roll back route if anything odd.

teresa: i'll run a quick smoke test plan against staging once PR is up. If you want, I can help with the drain + k8s cordon steps.

ashley: awesome — thanks. I'll add a checklist in the PR description and ping here before apply. :thumbsup:
